The 2023 Fisker Ocean is an all-electric five-seating small SUV from famed automotive designer Henrik Fisker. It's Fisker's first vehicle and is designed to be sustainable and emotional -- made with recycled and bio-based materials, and it has rooftop solar panels! ''The tide is turning for electric vehicles as an influx of new models flood the market, and Fisker looks to capitalize on that sentiment with its aptly named Ocean SUV,'' Car and Driver writes. Imagine: your power goes out and you're able to keep the lights on with your car. The Fisker Ocean also features a 150-kilowatt Combined Charging Standard (CCS) plug for DC fast charging. Thirty minutes of charging will add more than 200 miles of driving (based on charging the battery pack from 15% to 80%). The 17.1-inch Revolve center screen rotates, swiveling from a Control mode (portrait view) to a Hollywood mode (landscape view) with a 16:9 widescreen format. The landscape format allows users to enjoy movies and videos, complete with 360-degree sound, in an immersive cinematic experience. Presumably, while not driving.'' U.S. News & World Report further expands on its 10 coolest features.   • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Rear camera - Watching your back! The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. The rear camera is an extra set of eyes that's both convenient and safe.
Technology and Telematics

Theres a kind of compact menace to the 2025 BMW M2 that reads like a love letter to intent. Its small in stature and vast in attitudeproportions honed to a single, thrilling purpose. The silhouette sits low and taut, shoulders flaring with deliberate muscle, and every crease seems to point toward the next corner. Up close, the face wears an aggressive calm: gills and intakes that look purposeful rather than ornamental, a grille that pins its gaze forward, and a stance so unapologetically planted it feels like it could harvest pavement.

Slide inside and the M2s character shifts from exterior bravado to intimate focus. The cockpit is compact, crafted around the driver as if to say, Here, take control. Seats hold with confident firmness, stitching and bolsters that feel more like coaching than comfort. Surfaces pair purposeful tactility with bold flashes of trim, switchgear has the satisfying resistance of things designed to be used, not admired. Its a cabin that rewards concentrationsimple in layout, rich in nuance, with human-scaled ergonomics that make the act of driving feel like a practiced ritual.

On the road the M2 is immediacy made mechanical. It responds with an eager, unapologetic clarity: turn-in is sharp, throttle answers like a kept promise, and the chassis translates intent into motion with surgical precision. There is a delicious directness to the steering that communicates exactly what the tarmac is doing beneath you, and the suspension strikes a rare compromisealive and articulate without being punishing. When you ask for momentum, the M2 obliges with an excited, controlled surge that reads as enthusiasm rather than aggression.

The soundtrack is mischievous, a growl that warms into an insistent tenor when pushed, punctuating shifts and moments of bravado with character. Cabin sound is alive but not intrusiveevery rise and crackle feels like punctuation to a conversation between car and driver.

Practicalities exist but never dominate, the M2 is about moments rather than errands. It is a compact manifesto: visceral, composed, and unashamedly focused on engagement. For someone who values a car that rewards commitment, the 2025 M2 feels less like a vehicle and more like a compact, beautifully tuned provocationurgent, precise, and endlessly eager to be asked something interesting.

    • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
    • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.

2023 PORSCHE CAYENNE TURBO GT

BURMESTER SOUND SYSTEM, PORSCHE INNODRIVE, HEAD-UP DISPLAY, AND MORE!

OVERVIEW
The 2023 Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT isn't simply a Cayenne with more power––it's a meticulously tuned machine that dominates both road and track. As the flagship of its SUV lineup, the Turbo GT embodies Porsche's relentless pursuit of speed, precision, and everyday usability. Under the hood lies a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8, pushing out an astonishing 631 horsepower and 626 lb-ft of torque. Mated to a lightning-quick 8-speed Tiptronic S transmission and Porsche's AWD system, the Turbo GT sprints to 60 mph in just 3.1 seconds and on to a top speed of 189 mph––numbers once reserved only for supercars. A titanium exhaust system, active chassis controls, and Porsche Active Suspension Management ensure an equally thrilling soundtrack and driving experience. Exterior styling is as aggressive as its performance suggests, with 22-inch GT Design wheels, carbon-fiber roof, enlarged air intakes, and an adaptive rear spoiler. Massive carbon-ceramic brakes provide more than ample stopping power. Inside, the cabin blends luxury with motorsport focus: perforated Alcantara trimmed sport seats, deviated stitching, front & rear heated seats, and a driver-centric digital cockpit create an environment built for speed yet tailored for comfort. As with many Porsches, customization is key. Some standout features on this Cayenne Turbo GT include: Porsche Innodrive, a Burmester Sound System, a surround view camera, and sunblinds for rear passengers. Whether carving through winding roads or simply making the school run unforgettable, the Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT delivers a driving experience unlike any other SUV on the road.

The 2025 Rolls-Royce Cullinan takes the concept of ultra-luxury SUV travel and elevates it to a new plane––and this English White example is a testament to the brand's near-limitless capacity for bespoke craftsmanship. Step into the Cullinan's tricolor leather interior and you'll be greeted by climate controlled massaging seats complemented by Piano Black veneer. Technology is seamlessly integrated as well, with blind spot monitoring, a head-up display, and a surround view camera. Additional standouts include a shooting star headliner, rear seat infotainment screens, and a mini spirit of ecstasy perched beneath the clock. In a world filled with luxury, the Rolls-Royce Cullinan still stands alone––and this example makes it clear why: it's a rolling expression of taste and distinction, meticulously crafted for the discerning driver who demands exclusivity and artistry in every detail.

It detects prolonged driver unresponsiveness, automatically bringing the vehicle to a stop and turning on the hazard lights. If equipped, emergency services will also be contacted. Unresponsive driver assistant is safety that never sleeps.

  • Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety.   • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians.
